rationale.conceptual: The paper introduces a custom three-step alignment method combining classical MD snapshots, hydronium insertion into liquid water, and semiconductor-water interface Hartree potential averaging. Reproducing the results requires translating this method into code, understanding the physical rationale (band alignment, electrostatic potentials, CBM vs LUMO), and correctly setting up several interconnected DFT calculations across six materials. It is not a textbook recipe but a research-grade protocol that demands domain expertise.
rationale.execution: The workflow has seven sequential stages: (1) classical MD of water with LAMMPS and TIP4P, (2) DFT consistency validation of snapshots, (3) isolated hydronium relaxation, (4) hydronium insertion and acceptor level calculation (four configurations), (5) bulk semiconductor DFT (six materials), (6) interfacial slab supercell constructions and Hartree potential averaging, (7) final combination of terms. It requires orchestrating two different software packages (LAMMPS, GPAW), generating appropriate input structures and pseudopotentials, managing convergence, and handling many file I/Os. This is a long, fragile pipeline with multiple load‑bearing handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The method is a multi-component first-principles protocol (classical MD + DFT-GGA/PBE with PAW, hydronium insertion, bulk and interfacial slab calculations) that requires deep understanding of solid-state physics, electrostatics, and computational setup; it is clearly research-grade and non-trivial to implement correctly. The pipeline spans seven inter-dependent stages with two different simulation codes and careful input preparation, orchestration, and convergence handling. Resource needs are moderate: small DFT cells (≈128 atoms water, slab supercells) so no GPU required, modest RAM (∼16 GB) and tiny input data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations involve small unit cells (≈128 atoms of water) and slab supercells of moderate size, using plane-wave codes typical of CPU-only compute; no GPU needed. Peak RAM is on the order of 16 GB for a few hundred atom cells. Input files (crystal structures from literature) are negligible in size.
